questions.question: Under the 2018 amendments in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy approved by the Cabinet, the maximum Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) permitted under the automatic route in Single Brand Retail Trading (SBRT) is _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2018**, the **Union Cabinet**, chaired by the Prime Minister, approved several amendments in the **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** policy to simplify and liberalize the regime for investors.
 
• The most notable change was permitting **100% FDI** under the **automatic route** for **Single Brand Retail Trading (SBRT)**, which eliminated the need for **Government approval** for investments exceeding **49%**.
 
• Before this amendment, while **100% FDI** was allowed in **SBRT**, only up to **49%** could be brought in via the **automatic route**, and any stake beyond that required approval from the **Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB)** or its successor bodies.
 
• The policy move was designed to improve the **Ease of Doing Business** in India, encouraging global brands like **Apple**, **IKEA**, and **Nike** to set up wholly-owned subsidiaries and retail stores directly.
 
• **Single Brand Retail Trading** involves the sale of products that are sold under the same brand name globally and are branded during manufacturing, ensuring a uniform consumer experience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Local Sourcing Norms**:

 
 
• For entities with more than **51% FDI** in **SBRT**, there is a mandatory requirement to source **30%** of the value of goods from India, preferably from **MSMEs** and local artisans.
 
• The 2018 policy allowed incremental sourcing for global operations by the brand entity to be set off against the **30% local sourcing** requirement for a period of five years.
 
 
 
• **FDI Routes in India**:
 
 
• **Automatic Route**: The non-resident investor or the Indian company does not require any prior approval from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** or the **Government of India**.
 
• **Government Route**: Prior approval is mandatory through the **Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP)**, managed by the **DPIIT** under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
 
 
• **Policy Impact**:
 
 
• These reforms aimed to boost **domestic manufacturing**, generate **employment**, and provide Indian consumers with access to a wider variety of global products and technologies.

questions.question: The Constitution of India provided for how many types of emergencies in Part XVIII, from Articles 352 to 360?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** delineates extraordinary provisions under **Part XVIII**, spanning from **Articles 352 to 360**, to deal with situations that threaten the security and stability of the nation.
 
• The first type is a **National Emergency**, governed by **Article 352**, which can be declared by the **President of India** if there is a grave threat to the security of India or any part thereof due to **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**.
 
• The second type is the **State Emergency**, popularly known as **President's Rule**, under **Article 356**. It is invoked when the **constitutional machinery** in a state fails, or under **Article 365** if a state fails to comply with directions from the **Union government**.
 
• The third type is a **Financial Emergency**, outlined in **Article 360**, which the **President** may proclaim if the **financial stability** or credit of India, or any part of its territory, is deemed to be in immediate danger.
 
• These provisions effectively transform the **federal structure** of the Indian political system into a **unitary** one, allowing the **Central Government** to exercise supreme authority to manage the crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Procedural Characteristics and History**

 
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** introduced significant safeguards, such as requiring a **written recommendation** from the **Cabinet** for a **National Emergency** and replacing the term 'internal disturbance' with **'armed rebellion'**.
 
• While a **National Emergency** has been declared three times in India (1962, 1971, and 1975), a **Financial Emergency** under **Article 360** has never been invoked since the inception of the Constitution.
 
• Under **Article 359**, the **President** has the power to suspend the right to approach the courts for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**, except those guaranteed under **Articles 20 and 21**.
 
• The concept of emergency provisions in the Indian Constitution is heavily influenced by the **Government of India Act, 1935**, and the **Weimar Constitution of Germany** regarding the suspension of rights.

questions.question: The NAVYA (Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls) initiative, launched on 24 June 2025, is for which age group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16 - 18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NAVYA** (**Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls**) initiative was officially launched on **24 June 2025**.
 
• The program specifically targets adolescent girls in the age group of **16 - 18 years**, a vital demographic that is often at risk of dropping out of the formal education system.
 
• The primary goal of the initiative is to provide specialized **vocational training** and **skill development** to empower young women and enhance their future **employability**.
 
• The scheme focuses on bridging the gap between **academic learning** and **industry requirements**, ensuring that girls are equipped with market-relevant skills before they enter the professional world.
 
• By focusing on this specific age bracket, **NAVYA** aims to foster **economic independence** and provide a sense of direction to young girls during their formative years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Goals of the Initiative**:

 
 
• The program aligns with the **Skill India Mission** and the **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** framework to improve **gender parity** in the labor force.
 
• Training modules often include **digital literacy**, **healthcare assistance**, **textiles**, and **Information Technology** (IT) services.
 
• Participants receive **certification** upon completion, which is recognized by various **industrial sectors** and **government bodies**.
 
 
 
• **Social and Economic Impact**:
 
 
• Focusing on the **16 - 18 years** age group helps in delaying the age of **marriage** and reducing **maternal mortality** by keeping girls engaged in productive learning.
 
• The initiative also includes **life skills** training, such as **financial literacy**, **self-defense**, and **effective communication**, to build overall confidence.
 
• It targets **rural** and **underprivileged urban** areas to ensure that the benefits of **vocational education** reach the most vulnerable populations.

questions.question: Which country launched the first indigenous, Low-Cost Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease, named "BIRSA 101"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** has achieved a significant milestone in medical biotechnology by launching **BIRSA 101**, its first **indigenous, low-cost gene therapy** specifically designed to treat **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**.
 
• The therapy was developed through the collaborative efforts of premier institutions, including the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** and the **Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (IGIB)**, highlighting India’s growing capability in **gene-editing** technologies.
 
• The name **BIRSA** is a tribute to the legendary tribal leader **Birsa Munda**, reflecting the primary target of this medical intervention, as **Sickle Cell Disease** disproportionately affects **tribal communities** across the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• This therapy utilizes **CRISPR-Cas9** technology to correct the genetic mutation in **hemoglobin**, offering a potential one-time cure that is significantly more affordable than international alternatives which can cost upwards of 2 to 3 million dollars.
 
• By localizing the production and clinical trial process, India aims to provide life-saving treatment to thousands of patients who previously had no access to advanced **genomic medicine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**:

 
 
• It is a **hereditary blood disorder** where red blood cells assume an abnormal, rigid, sickle shape, leading to **anemia**, organ damage, and severe pain crises.
 
• The **Government of India** launched the **National Sickle Cell Anemia Elimination Mission** in **2023**, with the ambitious goal of eliminating the disease by the year **2047**.
 
 
 
• **Gene Therapy Landscape**:
 
 
• Traditional treatments were limited to **blood transfusions** and **bone marrow transplants**, which are often risky or unavailable to the masses.
 
• The **BIRSA 101** initiative represents a shift toward **personalized medicine** and high-end **molecular therapeutics** within the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) framework.

questions.question: Which bank joins the India Bullion Exchange as a special category client?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)** has achieved a milestone by becoming the first **Public Sector Bank (PSB)** to join the **India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX)** as a **Special Category Client (SCC)**.
 
• The **IIBX** is India's first International Bullion Exchange, situated in the **Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City)** in **Gandhinagar**, established to provide a transparent platform for bullion trading.
 
• As an **SCC**, **SBI** is empowered to participate directly in the exchange to facilitate the **import of gold** and **silver** for its domestic clients, specifically **Qualified Jewellers**.
 
• This participation follows the regulatory framework set by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA)**, which allows **Scheduled Commercial Banks** to act as intermediaries in the bullion market.
 
• The integration of **SBI** into the **IIBX** ecosystem is expected to significantly increase **trading volumes** and provide better **price discovery** for the Indian bullion market, which is one of the largest in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX)**:

 
 
• Inaugurated in **July 2022**, it aims to make India a price setter rather than a price taker in the global **bullion** market.
 
• The exchange offers various products, including **Gold 995** and **Gold 999** purity, along with **Silver** contracts.
 
 
 
• **Special Category Client (SCC)** framework:
 
 
• Introduced by the **RBI** in **May 2022** to allow Indian banks to operate as **Professional Clearing Members** or **Trading Members** at **GIFT-IFSC**.
 
• Banks must maintain a minimum **Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)** as per **Basel III** norms to qualify for this status.
 
 
 
• **GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City)**:
 
 
• It serves as India's first **International Financial Services Centre (IFSC)**, designed to compete with global financial hubs like **Singapore**, **Dubai**, and **London**.
 
• It provides a **tax-neutral** environment and a streamlined regulatory regime for international financial entities.

questions.question: Under the new scheme for first-time Women, SC and ST entrepreneurs, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the **maximum loan amount** that can be availed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the Government of India announced a significant enhancement of financial support targeted at **first-time entrepreneurs** to foster a robust startup ecosystem.
 
• The scheme specifically prioritizes individuals from the **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **Women** categories to ensure **inclusive economic growth** and social equity.
 
• Under this revamped initiative, the maximum loan amount that can be availed by eligible entrepreneurs has been increased to **₹2 crore** per borrower.
 
• The primary objective of increasing the limit to **₹2 crore** is to support **greenfield enterprises** in manufacturing, services, or the trading sector, allowing for higher **capital expenditure**.
 
• This measure is part of the broader **Viksit Bharat** strategy, aimed at empowering marginalized sections to become **job creators** rather than job seekers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26**, presented by Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman**, emphasizes four key pillars: **Garib** (Poor), **Mahilayen** (Women), **Yuva** (Youth), and **Annadata** (Farmer).

 
 
• **Credit Guarantee Support**: To facilitate these high-value loans of up to **₹2 crore**, the government provides **credit guarantee covers**, reducing the risk for lending institutions like **Scheduled Commercial Banks**.
 
• **Entrepreneurship Promotion**: This enhancement follows the success of earlier versions of the **Stand-Up India** scheme, which previously had a lower ceiling, thereby reflecting the rising costs of technology and machinery.
 
• **Ease of Access**: The scheme is integrated with the **Jan Samarth Portal**, enabling a digital and transparent application process to improve the **Ease of Doing Business** for new entrants.
 
• **Economic Impact**: By targeting **first-time entrepreneurs**, the government aims to stimulate the **MSME sector**, which contributes significantly to India’s **GDP** and export earnings.

questions.question: Division of legislative subjects into union, state and concurrent List is contained in which of the following schedules of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** establishes the **federal distribution of powers** between the **Union** and the **States**.
 
• It is divided into three distinct lists: **List I (Union List)**, **List II (State List)**, and **List III (Concurrent List)**.
 
• **Article 246** serves as the constitutional basis for this schedule, defining the **legislative jurisdiction** of **Parliament** and **State Legislatures**.
 
• **List I (Union List)** currently comprises **100 subjects** (originally 97) such as **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, **Atomic Energy**, **Banking**, and **Communication**, where the Central Government holds exclusive authority.
 
• **List II (State List)** consists of **61 subjects** (originally 66) including **Public Order**, **Police**, **Public Health**, and **Agriculture**, governed primarily by state governments.
 
• **List III (Concurrent List)** features **52 subjects** (originally 47) like **Education**, **Forests**, **Marriage**, and **Criminal Law**, allowing both the **Union** and **States** to legislate, though central laws prevail in case of conflict.
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976** famously transferred five subjects from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List** to promote uniformity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fifth Schedule**:

 
 
• Contains provisions related to the **administration** and control of **Scheduled Areas** and **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• It excludes the tribal areas of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**, which are covered under the **Sixth Schedule**.
 
 
 
• **Ninth Schedule**:
 
 
• Introduced by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act (1951)** to protect **land reform** laws and other regulations from **judicial scrutiny**.
 
• Laws included here were initially immune to challenges regarding **Fundamental Rights** violations.
 
 
 
• **Eleventh Schedule**:
 
 
• Added by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992)** to empower **Panchayati Raj Institutions**.
 
• It lists **29 functional items** intended to promote **rural development** and **local self-governance**.

questions.question: Which dance form is performed by men wearing long colorful robes and tall conical caps in Jammu & Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dumhal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dumhal** is a prestigious folk dance originating from the **Jammu and Kashmir** region, specifically performed by the **Wattal tribe** on special ceremonial occasions.
 
• The performance is exclusively conducted by **male dancers** who dress in **long, vibrant colorful robes** and wear distinctive **tall conical caps** that are frequently embellished with **beads and shells**.
 
• The dance is **ritualistic** in nature and begins only after a **banner** is ceremoniously planted into the ground at a designated spot, serving as the focal point for the dancers.
 
• Dancers move in a **graceful circular formation** around this banner, accompanied by the rhythmic beats of **large drums** known as the **Duff**, while the participants sing **folk choruses** in unison.
 
• Historically, this dance was performed to seek **divine intervention** or **blessings** during times of distress or for the fulfillment of specific community prayers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hikat**:

 
 
• It is a traditional folk dance of **Jammu and Kashmir** usually performed by **young girls and boys**.
 
• The dancers **interlock their arms** and spin in circles, maintaining **perfect balance** while dancing to the tunes of **Rabbi music**.
 
 
 
• **Chholiya**:
 
 
• A famous **martial art-style dance** originating from the **Kumaon region** of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is primarily a **sword dance** performed during **wedding processions** and is believed to **ward off evil spirits**.
 
 
 
• **HurkaBaul**:
 
 
• An **agricultural folk dance** associated with the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is performed during the cultivation of **paddy and maize**, where the name refers to **Hurka** (the percussion instrument) and **Baul** (the song structure).
